subject: Throughput headroom top-up & credit escrow proposal
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput headroom top-up & credit escrow proposal

Hi Sara —

Quick note following our call this morning: Acme expects a 10–14 day marketing spike in late June and wants a short-duration headroom so their checkout ML features don't throttle. They asked for two practical things: a temporary top-up of throughput (capacity headroom) and a predictable invoice path (no surprise overrun).

Proposed quick option from our side:
- 2-week headroom: 50M additional tokens reserved (to be used only during the spike)
- One-off facilitation fee to reserve capacity: $2,750
- Usage during the top-up billed at standard hosted rates; any unused portion converts into a one-time credit at 70% of purchase price applied to the next invoice
- Optional: escrow the facilitation fee and the reserved-credit in a short-term invoice hold (we can split it across two invoices)

I attached a draft invoice and a usage snapshot for May to show ramp. Ben and Karthik are looped for pricing/legal follow-up.

If this works, we can produce a short amendment (SOW/Invoice) and get signatures via DocuSign.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189

Attachments: topup_invoice_draft.pdf (PDF), usage_snapshot_May2026.csv (CSV)
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@acme-retail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput headroom top-up & credit escrow proposal

Thanks, Priya — this looks close. A couple quick clarifications before I loop procurement: 

1) Can we confirm the exact token price that applies to usage consumed during the top-up window versus the facilitation fee? We bill-back internally and need line items.
2) Is the 70% unused conversion a hard floor or negotiable? Our finance team prefers amortizing credit across the next three invoices rather than a single credit line item.
3) What happens if the spike exceeds the reserved 50M tokens? Will we be automatically throttled or moved to a higher-rate emergency uplift?

If you can send me the SOW/short amendment language and the DocuSign link, we can push this through procurement quickly.

—Sara
Sara Chen
Head of Engineering (Retail) — Acme Retail
sara.chen@acme-retail.com

Sara — thanks for the questions, quick answers inline: 

1) Token pricing: during the top-up window usage is billed at Acme's current hosted rate of $0.00065/token (standard tier). The facilitation/reservation fee is a one-time $2,750 operational fee and is separate from per-token usage. We'll put both line items on the amendment so accounting can map it.

2) Credit conversion: the 70% is our standard short-term top-up conversion but is negotiable. For ACME I can offer a 80% conversion if you agree to amortize the credit over up to three invoices (we'll add language to the SOW). That means unused headroom converts to a credit equal to 80% of the unused dollar value and we apply it pro-rata over the next three billing cycles.

3) Overrun behavior: if you exceed the reserved 50M tokens we have two automations:
   - Primary: immediate soft-failover to your agreed emergency uplift rate (7% premium on standard hosted rate) to avoid dropping requests
   - Fallback: if the uplift rate pushes you beyond an internal safety threshold, requests will be routed to a compatible lower-cost model variant (downgrade path) until the commit is reset; we'll notify your billing and engineering contacts.

We can keep the soft-failover enabled for the two-week window and add a 30-day review after the spike to reconcile actuals. I've attached a draft SOW and a sample invoice layout for procurement.

If that looks good I can kick off legal to prepare the amendment and DocuSign package.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: topup_invoice_draft.pdf, SOW_short_amendment.docx

Subject: Re: Throughput headroom top-up & credit escrow proposal

Thanks Ben — the 80% conversion with amortization is okay on our end. A few procurement asks before we sign: 

- Can the facilitation fee be split across two invoices (50% now, 50% in 30 days)?
- We need the uplift failover to be explicit in the amendment with a ceiling on the uplift rate (max 10% premium).
- Please add a 30-day post-spike evaluation clause and a single-point contact for billing adjustments.

If you can send the final DocuSign by EOD Tue we should be able to hit signatures on Wed and have the headroom in place by June 20.

—Sara
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput headroom top-up & credit escrow proposal

Internal note for the package we send to Acme: 
- Agree to split facilitation fee (50/50 across two invoices)
- Cap uplift premium at 10% for the two-week window; keep soft-failover and downgrade path as described
- Add a 30-day review and a clause that unconsumed headroom converts to an 80% credit applied pro-rata across next three invoices; include a short call-to-action for any disputes to be raised within 21 days of final reconciliation
- Add a one-paragraph operational runbook: how we enable the top-up (route config, thresholds, notification flow to Acme production-oncall)

I'll ask Legal to produce the amendment + DocuSign bundle today referencing deal D-2026-7889 and HubSpot record. Priya — want me to include the escrow wording (we'll hold facilitation fee on our side and release per invoice) or put it in the billing note?

—Karthik
